caption: Fig. 2.16 Energy level diagrams for the few electronic shells of (a) hydrogen atom and (b) multi-electronic atoms. Note that orbitals for the same value of principal quantum number, have the same energies even for different azimuthal quantum number for hydrogen atom. In case of multi-electron atoms, orbitals with same principal quantum number possess different energies for different azimuthal quantum numbers.
note: Two energy-level diagrams side by side, (a) on the left and (b) on the right, each with a vertical energy line and short red dashes for the levels (dashes and lines are artwork, not labels; there is no printed axis label). Labels are listed panel by panel - all of (a) then all of (b) - rather than by a strict whole-figure top-left-to-bottom-right sweep, which would interleave the two panels' levels and lose which atom each belongs to. Within each panel the order is top to bottom, left to right within a level band. In (a) the 3s, 3p and 3d dashes are printed at the same height (degenerate) and likewise 2s and 2p; in (b) the levels are staggered, with 4s printed below 3d. "3d", "3p", "3s", "2p", "2s" and "1s" each appear in both panels, which the flat list cannot distinguish. Excluded from the grown crop (outside target_box_in_crop): the paragraph above the panel ("...hydrogen atom, as said earlier, corresponds to the most stable condition ... excited state."), the whole right-hand column, and the footer "2024-25".
